pointers.sentence: The mark is made in `django/utils/safestring.py` and the escaping in `django/utils/html.py`; the engine applies them in `render_value_in_context`, in its filters, and as the `"autoescape"` option and `{% autoescape %}` direct.

The mark is made in `django/utils/safestring.py` and the escaping in `django/utils/html.py`; the engine applies them in `render_value_in_context`, in its filters, and as the `"autoescape"` option and `{% autoescape %}` direct.

`__html__` is a convention shared with other libraries: an object that has it can be asked for its HTML, and the docstring says it lets other template engines understand Django's safe data (`django/utils/safestring.py:SafeData`).
Every other string method is `str`'s own, so an upper-cased, sliced or replaced safe string is plain (`django/utils/safestring.py:SafeString`).
Wrapped in `keep_lazy`, it leaves a lazy translation lazy, to become a `SafeString` when it is evaluated (`django/utils/safestring.py:mark_safe`).
It escapes even what is escaped already (`django/utils/html.py:escape`).

`conditional_escape` is the one `render_value_in_context` uses: a lazy string is made a `str`, an object with `__html__` is asked for its HTML, and anything else goes to `escape` (`django/utils/html.py:conditional_escape`).

It works as `str.format`, passing each argument through `conditional_escape` and marking the result safe, so `format_html("
  • {}
    • ", ship)` puts a ship named `` in as `<Beagle>` and a safe argument as it stands (`django/utils/html.py:format_html`).

It wraps `__str__` so that its result is marked safe, and adds an `__html__` that returns `str(self)`; it refuses a class that defines `__html__` itself or does not itself define `__str__` (`django/utils/html.py:html_safe`).

`escapejs` replaces the backslash, quotes, angle brackets, some other punctuation, the Unicode line and paragraph separators and the control characters with escapes such as `"\u003C"`, for a value inside a JavaScript string, and marks the result safe (`django/utils/html.py:escapejs`).

`json_script` serialises a value, by default with `DjangoJSONEncoder`, escapes angle brackets and ampersands the same way, and wraps it in a `<script type="application/json">` element; its docstring calls the escaped JSON safe anywhere but inside a tag's attribute (`django/utils/html.py:json_script`).
With autoescaping off it only converts (`django/template/base.py:render_value_in_context`).
`{{ form }}` writes a form unescaped: its `__str__` is `RenderableMixin.render`, which marks the rendering safe (`django/forms/utils.py:RenderableMixin.render`).

`NodeList.render` joins its nodes' strings and marks the whole safe, so the template's own text, which a `TextNode` returns as it stands, goes out unescaped, and so does what a tag's node returns (`django/template/base.py:NodeList.render`).

What a tag writes is escaped only if its node escapes it: the node of a `simple_tag` passes its function's result through `conditional_escape` when autoescaping is on, as `{% url %}` does its URL (`django/template/library.py:SimpleNode.render`).
So `{{ "Valletta" }}` writes a bold Valletta, and for a port with none, `{{ port.harbourmaster|default:"vacant" }}` writes `"vacant"` (`django/template/base.py:Variable.__init__`).
When its input was safe, the engine marks its result safe; when not, the engine leaves the result as it is (`django/template/base.py:FilterExpression.resolve`).

It converts the first argument by `str`, which keeps a `SafeString` safe and turns an object whose `__str__` returns a safe string into one, then makes the engine's test on the converted value, reading `is_safe=True` from the innermost function, where `Library.filter` also sets it (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:stringfilter`).

With two ships, `{{ names|join:"
" }}` writes `"Endeavour
<Beagle>"`, the separator being a literal, and safe (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:join`).
Whether to escape is a property of the context, `Context.autoescape`, an attribute beside the stack, true by default (`django/template/context.py:Context`).

The engine's `"autoescape"` option, true unless `"OPTIONS"` says otherwise, reaches it through the backend's template, which makes its context with the engine's setting (`django/template/backends/django.py:Template.render`).

The compile function `autoescape` accepts `"on"` or `"off"` and nothing else; its `AutoEscapeControlNode` sets the context's attribute, renders its body, and puts the old value back (`django/template/defaulttags.py:AutoEscapeControlNode.render`).

The setting holds for all that renders with the context meanwhile: a filter's `autoescape` argument, a simple tag, an included template, even one included with `only`, since `BaseContext.new` copies the old context's attributes (`django/template/context.py:BaseContext.new`).

`{% filter %}` refuses `|escape` and `|safe` anywhere in its chain, naming `{% autoescape %}` instead, which its docstring calls the way to manage autoescaping for a block (`django/template/defaulttags.py:do_filter`).
These filters only escape or mark, each by a function of `django/utils/html.py` or `django/utils/safestring.py` ([The built-in filters](filters.md)).
